## Notebook Overview

**Inputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS estimates, one row per 2020 CA block group.
- `../../../data/xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather` — 2020 block group → 2010 tract allocation weights.
- Optional prior outputs in `../../../data/parity_reference` (§1.4) — separate
  schema and Southern California parity references for each product, including
  the product-specific filenames listed below.

**Outputs:**

- `../../../data/acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS measures aggregated to 2010 tracts (Southern California + Bay Area), with rental inventory (`rhu_inventoryE`), interpolated rent, missing- and top-coded-rent shares, share, vacancy-rate, and CV measures.


This notebook:

1. Set up environment
2. Assemble 2020–2024 ACS block-group measures to 2010 tracts
3. Validate outputs

Either Step 2 notebook can run first. [02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd](02a_aggregate_2024_block_groups.Rmd) produces the
block-group aggregate; [02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd](02b_prepare_tract_sources.Rmd) produces both native tract tables.
Both use `step2_target_counties()` in `R/geography_qa.R` (§1.3).
`04_merge.Rmd` consumes all three unchanged products for its hierarchical panel
and source diagnostics. No inventory MOE or CV is introduced.

# 1. Set up environment

## 1.1 Load packages

```{r load-packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())

library(here)          # project-root-relative paths via here::here()
library(Hmisc)
library(dplyr)
library(assertr)

library(survey)        # core survey analysis functions
library(srvyr)         # tidyverse-style wrapper for survey
library(forcats)
```

## 1.2 Load helper functions

This stage's helpers — feather I/O, the merge/filter helpers, the weighting and
aggregation functions, flagging functions, and diagnostic helpers — live in
`R/assemble_helpers.R`. That file is self-contained for this notebook (it carries
its own `summ_var()`, distinct from the one used by `01_acs.Rmd`).
Shared geographic, key, schema, and parity diagnostics live in `R/geography_qa.R`.

```{r load-helpers}
source(here::here("R", "assemble_helpers.R"))
source(here::here("R", "geography_qa.R"))
```

## 1.3 Set data directory and target counties

```{r set-paths}
# Trailing slash is intentional: save_data() builds paths with paste0().
data_dir <- "../../../data/"

county_config <- step2_target_counties()
southern_california_counties <- county_config$southern_california_counties
bay_area_counties <- county_config$bay_area_counties
target_counties <- county_config$target_counties

# Point to a preserved prior-output directory for repeatable analyst parity runs.
parity_reference_dir <- "../../../data/parity_reference"
```

## 1.4 Read prior outputs for parity checks

Prior outputs are read from `parity_reference_dir`, configured as
`../../../data/parity_reference`, before any output is saved. Preserve these
snapshots for repeated comparisons; saving candidates in `data_dir` does not
replace them. A missing reference is reported as **parity not checked**, never
as a pass. Reference and candidate must use the same statewide inputs and
measurement code, apart from the approved income correction and schema migration
below. Differences use a numeric tolerance of
`1e-10 * max(1, abs(prior), abs(candidate))`; shared column names, order, and
types must match exactly. Only `rhu_inventoryE` is joined from inventory
diagnostics into the Feathers.

### Decision: Permit only the agreed Step 2 schema migration

`compare_socal_parity()` remains strict by default (`schema_migration = NULL`).
This notebook opts into a fixed vintage-specific allowlist:

| `schema_migration` | Permitted additions | Permitted removals |
|---|---|---|
| `"2024"` (block-group aggregated only) | `rhu_inventoryE` | Low-rent counts; weighted rent/lower-quartile/value estimates and companions listed below |

The fixed 2024 block-group cleanup removes `rhu_lrE`, `rhu_lr2E`, `rentE`,
`rentM`, `rentCV`, `lqcrentE`, `lqcrentM`, `med_hvalE`, `med_hvalM`,
`med_hvalCV`, `hu_miss_hval`, and `pct_miss_hval`. Weighted income remains.
Native tract estimates and uncertainty remain unchanged. Retired fields are
rejected even when no parity reference exists.

Actual additions/removals appear in `schema_changes`; unlisted differences fail.
All shared columns retain the existing value, type, and order comparisons,
including the income and geographic classifications below. Inventory is validated
independently before saving and after reloading (§3.6), even when no reference
contains it. Save/reload schema comparison remains strict for every column.

### Decision: Verify the approved income correction against preserved references

The geographic parity check compares every shared output column. Only a changed
`med_hhincE` or `med_hhincCV` cell whose reference **and** candidate values match
the legacy and corrected expectations qualifies as `verified_income_correction`.
Expectations use inputs before censoring (§2.4), with the former
missing/top-coded-rent income exclusion applied only to the legacy estimate.
Both expected CVs use the reference `med_hhincM` and the existing
`(med_hhincM / 1.645) / med_hhincE` formula. Candidate MOEs remain subject to
ordinary parity. Missing values and numeric tolerance follow the same comparison
rule as all other columns. Without expectations, the helper remains strict.

### Decision: Keep source-specific references and preserve historical snapshots

The explicit map retains the historical `acs_step2_24.feather` snapshot for
this block-group product. It is never renamed or overwritten. An absent
reference leaves parity unchecked.

```{r load-parity-references}
parity_reference_files <- c(
  "2024_bg_aggregated" = "acs_step2_24.feather"
)
prior_outputs <- read_step2_parity_references(parity_reference_dir, parity_reference_files)
```

# 2. Assemble 2020–2024 ACS block-group measures to 2010 tracts

## 2.1 Import block-group ACS and crosswalk

### Decision: Discard retired low-rent counts from older inputs

All three ACS input paths drop `rhu_lrE` and `rhu_lr2E` if an older cache still
contains them. These counts are no longer constructed in Step 1. Source rent
estimates and every gross-rent bin remain available; no source rows are removed.

```{r import-bg-and-xwalk-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Load 2024 ACS block group data
acs_2024_bg_source <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "acs_step1_2024_block_group.feather") |>
  select(-any_of(step2_cleanup_columns("2016")))
report_n(acs_2024_bg_source, "2024 ACS block-group sources loaded")

# acs_2024_bg_source <- acs_2024_bg_source |>
#   mutate(rentE=ifelse(rentE>3501,NA, rentE))

# Bring in crosswalk
xwalk <- load_data(data_dir, NULL, "xwalk_bg24_tr10.feather")
report_n(xwalk, "bg2020->tr2010 crosswalk loaded")
```

## 2.2 Select destination tracts and merge all contributing block groups

### Decision: Define the sample by destination 2010 tracts

Keep every crosswalk row whose **destination** is in `target_counties`, including
sources outside those counties. The inspection documents cross-county allocations
that a source-county filter would lose. Join these rows to the statewide ACS
cache using their source IDs; every retained crosswalk row must match exactly
one ACS block group after the zero-weight exception below. Non-target
destinations are excluded before aggregation.

The original NHGIS weights describe fractions of each source allocated across
all destinations. Their full source sums must be within `1e-6` of one (allowing
crosswalk rounding). Retained fractions may sum to less than one when other
destinations lie outside the sample. **Do not renormalize them.** Relative MOE
weights in §2.3 retain their existing, separate definition.

### Decision: Exclude unmatched links only when all allocation weights are zero

The crosswalk includes a link from Nevada block group `320030057033` to
San Bernardino tract `06071010300` with all four weights exactly zero. That
source is absent from the California ACS cache, but the link contributes no
population, households, housing units, or renter units.

Report unmatched IDs and weights, then exclude only unmatched links whose four
weights are finite and exactly zero. Matched zero-weight links remain. Any
unmatched positive weight, however small, or missing/invalid weight still fails
validation. Remove the excluded pairs from both the join and its crosswalk
reference so the unchanged-weight check in §2.3 compares the same allocations.
Destination tract coverage must remain unchanged; no weights are renormalized.

```{r merge-and-restrict-2024-bg-aggregated}
assert_unique_key(acs_2024_bg_source, "bg2020_id", "Statewide 2024 ACS block groups")
assert_unique_key(xwalk, c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"), "Crosswalk allocation pairs")
xwalk_target <- select_target_counties(xwalk, tr2010_id, target_counties)
report_drop(xwalk_target, nrow(xwalk), "allocations to non-target destination tracts")
target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated <- unique(xwalk_target$tr2010_id)
source_ids <- distinct(xwalk_target, bg2020_id)

# Retain all destinations for these sources only to audit original weight sums.
xwalk_sources <- semi_join(xwalk, source_ids, by = "bg2020_id")
report_drop(xwalk_sources, nrow(xwalk), "sources with no target destination")
weight_cols <- c("wt_pop", "wt_hh", "wt_hu", "wt_renthu")
stopifnot("Crosswalk weights must be finite fractions" = all(vapply(
  xwalk_sources[weight_cols], function(w) all(is.finite(w) & w >= 0 & w <= 1), logical(1)
)))
source_weight_qa_2024_bg_aggregated <- bind_rows(
  mutate(xwalk_sources, allocation = "full"),
  mutate(xwalk_target, allocation = "retained")
) |>
  group_by(bg2020_id, allocation) |>
  summarise(across(all_of(weight_cols), sum), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(weight_cols), names_to = "weight", values_to = "fraction") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = allocation, values_from = fraction)
source_weight_qa_2024_bg_aggregated |>
  group_by(weight) |>
  summarise(sources = n(), min_full = min(full), max_full = max(full),
            min_retained = min(retained), max_retained = max(retained),
            partially_retained = sum(retained < full - 1e-6), .groups = "drop") |>
  print(n = Inf, width = Inf)
stopifnot("Full source weights must sum to one" = all(abs(source_weight_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$full - 1) <= 1e-6),
          "Retained weights cannot exceed original weights" =
            all(source_weight_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$retained <= source_weight_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$full + 1e-6))

# Coverage diagnostic only: this does not select the allocation sample.
sources_without_xwalk <- select_target_counties(acs_2024_bg_source, bg2020_id, target_counties) |>
  anti_join(distinct(xwalk, bg2020_id), by = "bg2020_id")
report_n(sources_without_xwalk, "Target-county ACS sources missing from the crosswalk (expected 0)")
stopifnot(nrow(sources_without_xwalk) == 0L)

acs_sources <- semi_join(acs_2024_bg_source, source_ids, by = "bg2020_id")
report_drop(acs_sources, nrow(acs_2024_bg_source), "ACS sources with no target destination")
xwalk_join <- merge_df(xwalk_target, acs_sources, "bg2020_id")
table(xwalk_join$merge)
stopifnot("Crosswalk join must not multiply allocation pairs" =
            nrow(xwalk_join) == nrow(xwalk_target))

xwalk_join_filt <- xwalk_join |>
  filter(merge == "left_only")
print(select(xwalk_join_filt, bg2020_id, tr2010_id, all_of(weight_cols)),
      n = Inf, width = Inf)
zero_weight_unmatched <- xwalk_join_filt |>
  filter(if_all(all_of(weight_cols), ~ is.finite(.x) & .x == 0)) |>
  select(bg2020_id, tr2010_id, all_of(weight_cols))

n_before <- nrow(xwalk_target)
xwalk_target <- anti_join(xwalk_target, zero_weight_unmatched,
                          by = c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"))
report_drop(xwalk_target, n_before, "unmatched zero-weight allocations from the reference")
n_before <- nrow(xwalk_join)
xwalk_join <- anti_join(xwalk_join, zero_weight_unmatched,
                        by = c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"))
report_drop(xwalk_join, n_before, "unmatched zero-weight allocations from the join")
stopifnot("Every retained target allocation must match one ACS source" =
            all(xwalk_join$merge == "both"),
          "Retained join and crosswalk must have the same row count" =
            nrow(xwalk_join) == nrow(xwalk_target),
          "Excluding zero-weight links must preserve target tract coverage" =
            setequal(xwalk_target$tr2010_id, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated))
assert_unique_key(xwalk_join, c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id"), "Matched allocation pairs")

n_before <- nrow(xwalk_join)
acs_2024_bg_allocations <- xwalk_join |>
  dplyr::filter(merge == "both") |>
  select(-c(merge))
report_drop(acs_2024_bg_allocations, n_before, "unmatched target allocations (expected 0)")

# Record newly included sources for the Southern California parity audit.
socal_boundary_contributions_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
  select_target_counties(tr2010_id, southern_california_counties) |>
  filter(substr(bg2020_id, 1, 2) != "06" |
           !substr(bg2020_id, 3, 5) %in% southern_california_counties) |>
  transmute(tr2010_id, bg2020_id, across(all_of(weight_cols)),
            allocated_pop = popE * wt_pop, allocated_hh = hhE * wt_hh,
            allocated_hu = huE * wt_hu, allocated_rhu = rhuE * wt_renthu)
print(socal_boundary_contributions_2024_bg_aggregated, n = Inf, width = Inf)
socal_boundary_ids_2024_bg_aggregated <- unique(socal_boundary_contributions_2024_bg_aggregated$tr2010_id)

# Check missing data + margin of error
check_moe_vars <- c("rhuE", "rentE")

check_moe_out_2024_bg_aggregated <- map_dfr(check_moe_vars, ~summ_var(acs_2024_bg_allocations, .x))
check_moe_out_2024_bg_aggregated

# Check missing, top-coded
check_tc_vars <- c("rentE")

check_tc_out_2024_bg_aggregated <- map_dfr(check_tc_vars, ~check_tc(acs_2024_bg_allocations, .x))
check_tc_out_2024_bg_aggregated

rm(xwalk, xwalk_sources, xwalk_join, xwalk_join_filt, acs_2024_bg_source, acs_sources)
```

## 2.3 Compute relative weights and top-code diagnostics

### Decision: Relative weights for margin-of-error aggregation

Count estimates are aggregated with the NHGIS allocation weights directly, but
count margins of error are combined as a weighted root-sum-of-squares. For that we need
each block group's *relative* contribution to its tract total — `rel_wt_*` —
computed as the block group's weighted count over the tract's weighted total
(separately by population, housing units, and renter-occupied housing units).

### Decision: Retain the tract-level top-coded-rent share

`calc_pct_tc_m()` computes, on the **uncensored** block-group rent, two tract-level
shares of weighted renter-occupied units: the share that are top-coded (`pct_tc_rent`) and
the share that are truly missing (`pct_m_rent`). We keep `pct_tc_rent` on the
output — analogous to `pct_miss_rent` (§2.6) — so the top-coded portion of the
missing-rent share is auditable downstream. It must be computed here, *before*
censoring (§2.4): censoring sets top-coded `rentE` to `NA`, after which top-codes
can no longer be distinguished from genuine non-response.

```{r relative-weights-and-tc-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Calc the relative weight for count variables
acs_2024_bg_allocations <- calc_rel_wt(acs_2024_bg_allocations, tr2010_id)

# Allocation pairs and raw fractions must remain identical after selection/join.
allocation_columns <- c("bg2020_id", "tr2010_id", weight_cols)
stopifnot("Original allocation weights must be preserved exactly" = identical(
  acs_2024_bg_allocations |> select(all_of(allocation_columns)) |> arrange(bg2020_id, tr2010_id),
  xwalk_target |> select(all_of(allocation_columns)) |> arrange(bg2020_id, tr2010_id)
))

# Calculate top-coded vars
tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_pct_tc_m(acs_2024_bg_allocations, tr2010_id)
assert_tract_keys(tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated rent shares")
rent_shares_2024_bg_aggregated <- tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated

# County shares use allocated renter-occupied units and uncensored source rent.
rent_allocation_qa_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
  group_by(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5)) |>
  summarise(
    source_block_groups = n_distinct(bg2020_id),
    allocated_rhu = sum(rhuE * wt_renthu, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_rhu = sum(is.na(rentE) * rhuE * wt_renthu, na.rm = TRUE),
    topcoded_rhu = sum((!is.na(rentE) & rentE >= 3500) * rhuE * wt_renthu, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(missing_share = if_else(allocated_rhu > 0, missing_rhu / allocated_rhu, NA_real_),
         topcoded_share = if_else(allocated_rhu > 0, topcoded_rhu / allocated_rhu, NA_real_))

check_tc_vars <- c("pct_m_rent", "pct_tc_rent")
check_tc_out_2024_bg_aggregated <- map_dfr(check_tc_vars, ~summ_var(tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated, .x))
check_tc_out_2024_bg_aggregated

# Create top-coded flag
tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated <- tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated |>
    mutate (tc_flag_rent_24= if_else(!is.na(pct_tc_rent) & pct_tc_rent>0, 1, 0)) |>
    # Keep pct_tc_rent (top-coded-rent share, analogous to pct_miss_rent) alongside the flag
    select(tr2010_id, pct_tc_rent, tc_flag_rent_24)

table(tc_diagnostics_2024_bg_aggregated$tc_flag_rent_24)
```

## 2.4 Censor top-coded values and build structure-type aggregates

### Decision: Censor top-coded rent to missing

The ACS top-codes median gross rent (and the lower contract-rent quartile) at
$3,500. The shared censoring helper still sets these source values `>= 3500`
to `NA`. Censored source rent supplies the retained missing-rent diagnostics;
no weighted rent or lower-quartile estimate is constructed. A tract-level
top-code flag (`tc_flag_rent_24`, built in §2.3) records where censoring occurred.

### Decision: Retain income independently of rent censoring

The analyst specified that missing or top-coded rent must not make otherwise
available median household income missing. `censor_tc_vars()` therefore leaves
`med_hhincE` unchanged, preserving its source values and missingness. No separate
income threshold is introduced. In §2.5 the existing household-weighted mean
uses all available income contributions with the same allocation weights,
including contributions whose rent is missing or censored. This corrects the
previous helper's unintended exclusion of those incomes and can change both
tract income estimates and their CVs. See the
[income-censoring decision and validation](notes/income_censoring.md).

Before censoring, calculate both income expectations with the existing
`hhE * wt_hh` household allocation weights. The reference-MOE join must be
many-to-one and preserve every destination tract; these diagnostics stay
separate from the production table. Missing references leave expectations unset.

```{r income-expectations-2024-bg-aggregated}
expected_income_2024_bg_aggregated <- NULL
if (!is.null(prior_outputs[["2024_bg_aggregated"]])) {
  expected_income_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
    mutate(legacy_med_hhincE = if_else(is.na(rentE) | rentE >= 3500,
                                      NA_real_, med_hhincE)) |>
    group_by(tr2010_id) |>
    summarise(
      legacy_med_hhincE = weightedMean(legacy_med_hhincE, w = hhE * wt_hh, na.rm = TRUE),
      corrected_med_hhincE = weightedMean(med_hhincE, w = hhE * wt_hh, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    left_join(select(prior_outputs[["2024_bg_aggregated"]], tr2010_id, med_hhincM),
              by = "tr2010_id", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
    transmute(
      tr2010_id, legacy_med_hhincE, corrected_med_hhincE,
      legacy_med_hhincCV = (med_hhincM / 1.645) / legacy_med_hhincE,
      corrected_med_hhincCV = (med_hhincM / 1.645) / corrected_med_hhincE
    )
  assert_tract_keys(expected_income_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated income expectations")
}
```

```{r censor-and-structure-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Censor top-coded
summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$rentE)
acs_2024_bg_allocations <- censor_tc_vars(acs_2024_bg_allocations)
summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$rentE)

# Sum multifamily cagegories
acs_2024_bg_allocations <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
    mutate(mfE= mf_5_9E + mf_10_19E + mf_20_49E + mf_50E,
           smfE= sfd_attE +duplexE + quadplexE
    )
# summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$sfd_detE)
# summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$smfE)
# summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$mfE)
# summary(acs_2024_bg_allocations$huE)
```

## 2.5 Aggregate block groups to 2010 tracts

### Decision: Weighted aggregation from block groups to 2010 tracts

`calc_agg_vars()` collapses block groups to 2010 tracts using the allocation
weight appropriate to each measure:

- **Counts** (housing units, population, households, renter-occupied units, structure
  types, gross-rent categories): weighted **sums** — renter measures use
  `wt_renthu`, housing-unit/structure measures use `wt_hu`, population measures
  use `wt_pop`, household measures use `wt_hh`.
- **Median household income**: retain the weighted mean with `hhE * wt_hh`.
  Its MOE retains the existing weighted mean with `rhuE * wt_renthu`; the
  differing estimate/MOE weights are unchanged by this cleanup.
- **Count margins of error**: combined as `sqrt(sum((MOE * rel_wt)^2))` using
  the relative weights from §2.3.

Weighted gross rent, lower-quartile rent, and house value, their MOEs/CVs, and
house-value missingness diagnostics are no longer produced. This removal does
not change the income calculation, native tract measures, or rent bins.

This produces one row per 2010 tract.

```{r aggregate-to-tracts-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Calculate aggregate vars
n_bg <- nrow(acs_2024_bg_allocations)
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_agg_vars(acs_2024_bg_allocations, tr2010_id)
cat(sprintf("Aggregated %s block-group rows to %s tract rows\n",
            formatC(n_bg, format = "d", big.mark = ","),
            formatC(nrow(acs_2024_bg_aggregated), format = "d", big.mark = ",")))
assert_tract_keys(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated aggregated tracts")
allocated_counts_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
  group_by(tr2010_id) |>
  summarise(popE = sum(popE * wt_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
            hhE = sum(hhE * wt_hh, na.rm = TRUE),
            huE = sum(huE * wt_hu, na.rm = TRUE),
            rhuE = sum(rhuE * wt_renthu, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot("Tract counts must conserve their source contributions" = isTRUE(all.equal(
  acs_2024_bg_aggregated |> select(all_of(names(allocated_counts_2024_bg_aggregated))) |> arrange(tr2010_id),
  allocated_counts_2024_bg_aggregated |> arrange(tr2010_id), tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```

### Decision: Rename the 5+ multifamily count to `mf5E`

The aggregated multifamily count (`mfE = mf_5_9E + mf_10_19E + mf_20_49E +
mf_50E`) covers only structures with **five or more** units. We rename it to
`mf5E` so the 5+ cutoff is explicit in the column name and so it reads cleanly
alongside the combined non-single-family-attached measure built in §2.6. The
rename happens here, *after* `calc_agg_vars()`, because that aggregation function
expects the source column to be named `mfE`.

### Decision: Carry vacancy, owner-occupied, and small-multifamily counts up to tracts

`calc_agg_vars()` does not carry the for-rent / for-sale vacancy counts
(`vac_forrentE`, `vac_forsaleE`), owner-occupied units (`ohuE`), or the small-
multifamily count (`smfE`) up from block groups, but the vacancy-rate and
non-single-family measures in §2.6 need them at the tract level. We aggregate them
here as weighted **sums** using the housing-unit allocation weight `wt_hu` — the
same weight `calc_agg_vars()` uses for the other housing-unit counts (e.g.
`tot_vacE`) — and join them onto the tract table.

```{r aggregate-supplemental-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Rename the 5+ multifamily count so the aggregation cutoff is explicit
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_aggregated |>
  rename(mf5E = mfE)

# Weight-aggregate the counts calc_agg_vars() does not carry up (housing-unit
# weight wt_hu, matching tot_vacE), one row per 2010 tract
vac_owner_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
  group_by(tr2010_id) |>
  summarise(
    vac_forrentE = sum(vac_forrentE * wt_hu, na.rm = TRUE),
    vac_forsaleE = sum(vac_forsaleE * wt_hu, na.rm = TRUE),
    ohuE         = sum(ohuE * wt_hu, na.rm = TRUE),
    smfE         = sum(smfE * wt_hu, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join onto the aggregated tract table (expect every tract to match: all "both")
assert_tract_keys(vac_owner_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated supplemental counts")
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- merge_df(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, vac_owner_2024_bg_aggregated, "tr2010_id")
table(acs_2024_bg_aggregated$merge)
assert_complete_tract_join(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "Supplemental count join")
```

### Decision: Allocate all rental-inventory components with renter weights

Compute inventory separately from the source allocation rows in `acs_2024_bg_allocations`, after
the existing supplemental counts. `calc_rental_inventory()` validates numeric
estimate/MOE columns, geographic keys, unique allocation pairs, and finite
weights in [0, 1]. Observed estimates on positive-weight links must be finite
and nonnegative. Missing MOEs, income, or rent do not affect completeness.

For each destination, sum each component over retained links with `wt_renthu > 0`
using `sum(component * wt_renthu)` without removing missing values. The helper
records contributing-source and missing-component counts. If any contributing
estimate is `NA` or `NaN`, explicitly set `rhu_inventoryE = NA_real_`; otherwise
add the three diagnostic totals. A zero-contributor target has zero components,
zero inventory, and `inventory_incomplete = FALSE`. Retained weights are never
renormalized after excluding destinations or incomplete targets from QA totals.

The separate `inventory_rhuE`, `inventory_vac_forrentE`, and
`inventory_vac_rentedE` fields stay in `inventory_2024_bg_aggregated`. Existing `vac_forrentE`
continues to use `wt_hu` for vacancy rates; it cannot substitute for the
inventory's renter-weighted vacancy component. Existing `rhuE` and its
missing/top-coded-rent denominators remain occupied-renter measures.

```{r rental-inventory-2024-bg-aggregated}
inventory_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_rental_inventory(acs_2024_bg_allocations, tr2010_id, weight_col = "wt_renthu")
assert_tract_keys(inventory_2024_bg_aggregated, acs_2024_bg_aggregated$tr2010_id, "2024 block-group-aggregated inventory diagnostics")
inventory_missing_sources_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_allocations |>
  filter(wt_renthu > 0) |>
  select(tr2010_id, bg2020_id, wt_renthu, rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE) |>
  pivot_longer(c(rhuE, vac_forrentE, vac_rentedE),
               names_to = "missing_component", values_to = "estimate") |>
  filter(is.na(estimate))
print(inventory_missing_sources_2024_bg_aggregated, n = Inf, width = Inf)
inventory_county_qa_2024_bg_aggregated <- inventory_2024_bg_aggregated |>
  dplyr::count(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5), inventory_incomplete,
        zero_contributors = n_contributing == 0, name = "tracts")
print(inventory_county_qa_2024_bg_aggregated, n = Inf)

before_inventory_join <- acs_2024_bg_aggregated
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- left_join(
  acs_2024_bg_aggregated, select(inventory_2024_bg_aggregated, tr2010_id, rhu_inventoryE),
  by = "tr2010_id", relationship = "one-to-one"
)
report_n(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated inventory join (expected unchanged tract count)")
stopifnot("Inventory join must preserve every existing 2024 column and row" =
            identical(acs_2024_bg_aggregated[names(before_inventory_join)], before_inventory_join))
rm(before_inventory_join)
assert_rental_inventory(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, inventory_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated inventory after join")
inventory_reconciliation_2024_bg_aggregated <- reconcile_rental_inventory(
  acs_2024_bg_allocations, inventory_2024_bg_aggregated, tr2010_id, weight_col = "wt_renthu"
)
print(inventory_reconciliation_2024_bg_aggregated, width = Inf)
```

## 2.6 Derive interpolated rent, missingness, percentage, and CV measures

### Decision: Interpolated median rent within the median gross-rent category

We compute the block-group product's rent measure from its distribution,
locating the gross-rent category that contains the tract's median renter
household and linearly interpolating within that category's dollar bounds. The
bottom (`<$100`) and top (`$3,500+`) categories are open-ended, so tracts whose
median falls there (or with no cash-rent units) get `NA`. This construction is
unchanged by removal of the weighted-average rent estimate.

### Decision: Vacancy rates and the non-single-family-attached count

We add three structure/vacancy measures, defined identically for all three products:

- `nsfaE` — non-single-family **attached** units: `smfE + mf5E`
  (`sfd_att + duplex + quadplex` plus units in 5+ structures). Excludes
  single-family detached, mobile homes, and other units.
- `pctrvacE` — **rental vacancy rate**, the Census definition
  `vac_forrent / (renter-occupied + vac_forrent)`.
- `pctsvacE` — **for-sale vacancy rate**, `vac_forsale / (owner-occupied +
  vac_forsale)`.

Both rates are `NA` where the denominator is non-positive. Neither rate carries a
margin-of-error / CV column, matching the existing `pctvacE` overall-vacancy
share. `rhu_inventoryE` carries through these calculations unchanged and is not
used as a rate denominator or uncertainty input.

### Note: `pct_miss_rent` counts top-coded rent as missing

Top-coded `rentE` was censored to `NA` in §2.4 *before* this aggregation, so
`calc_missing_vars()` (which counts block groups where `rentE` is `NA`) treats both
genuinely missing and top-coded block groups as "missing." `pct_miss_rent` is
therefore the share of weighted renter units that are missing **or** top-coded,
and it decomposes as `pct_miss_rent ≈ pct_m_rent + pct_tc_rent` (truly missing
plus top-coded, both computed pre-censoring in §2.3). The retained `pct_tc_rent`
isolates the top-coded portion.

```{r derive-measures-2024-bg-aggregated}
# Calculate interpolated rent
interp_rent_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_interp_rent(acs_2024_bg_aggregated)
assert_tract_keys(interp_rent_2024_bg_aggregated, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "2024 block-group-aggregated interpolated rent")

# Calculate % missing vars
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_missing_vars(acs_2024_bg_aggregated)
summary(acs_2024_bg_aggregated$pct_miss_rent)

# Calculate % vars
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_pct_vars(acs_2024_bg_aggregated)

# Calculate MOE, CV
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- calc_cv(acs_2024_bg_aggregated, source = "bg_agg")

# Build the combined non-single-family-attached count and the rental / for-sale
# vacancy rates (see decision block above)
acs_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_aggregated |>
  mutate(
    nsfaE    = smfE + mf5E,
    pctrvacE = if_else((rhuE + vac_forrentE) > 0,
                       vac_forrentE / (rhuE + vac_forrentE), NA_real_),
    pctsvacE = if_else((ohuE + vac_forsaleE) > 0,
                       vac_forsaleE / (ohuE + vac_forsaleE), NA_real_)
  )
```

## 2.8 Save 2020–2024 block-group-aggregated output

**Output:** `acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated.feather` — 2020–2024 ACS measures aggregated to 2010
tracts (Southern California + Bay Area), including `rhu_inventoryE`. It replaces
the production filename `acs_step2_24.feather`; the legacy file is retained.
`04_merge.Rmd` consumes this filename for its canonical 2024 measures and diagnostics.

Before writing, assert county containment/coverage and keyed inventory
completeness, component totals, and range. Compare every shared output column
to the prior Southern California records, permitting the inventory addition
and fixed cleanup removals under `schema_migration = "2024"`. `socal_parity_2024_bg_aggregated` reports cell
differences and added/removed keys separately for unaffected and boundary tracts.
Each changed cell is classified as `verified_income_correction`,
`boundary_review`, or `unexpected`, with counts in `difference_summary` and all
values retained in `differences`. Every geographically unaffected difference
must be a verified income correction; other cell or membership changes fail.
The boundary group is defined by `socal_boundary_contributions_2024_bg_aggregated` (§2.2): incoming
sources omitted by the old source-county filter. Its differences require review
alongside those source weights/counts. Income corrections do not change that
geographic classification. Boundary exposure alone does not excuse unrelated
input changes.

```{r acceptance-2024-bg-aggregated}
report_tract_counties(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_interp, target_counties, "2024 block-group-aggregated destination counties")

  acs_2024_bg_aggregated_interp, prior_outputs[["2024_bg_aggregated"]], southern_california_counties,
  socal_boundary_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, expected_income = expected_income_2024_bg_aggregated, schema_migration = "2024"
)
```

# 3. Validate outputs

Re-loads the saved block-group output and checks key uniqueness, missingness on
critical variables, the encoding of the flag columns, and the distribution of
every numeric column. Inventory completeness and reconciliation repeat the
pre-save checks using the saved estimates and separate source diagnostics.

```{r reload-step2}
acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out <- arrow::read_feather(paste0(data_dir, "acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated.feather"))
```

## 3.1 Check key uniqueness and duplicates

Expected: the block-group output is unique on `tr2010_id`.

```{r validate-keys-step2}
cat("acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated:", nrow(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out), "rows |",
    n_distinct(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out$tr2010_id), "unique tr2010_id |",
    sum(duplicated(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out$tr2010_id)), "duplicate ids\n")
assert_tract_keys(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, target_tract_ids_2024_bg_aggregated, "Saved 2024 block-group-aggregated tract keys")
assert_same_schema(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, acs_2024_bg_aggregated_interp, "Saved 2024 block-group-aggregated schema")
assert_step2_cleanup(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, "2024")
```

## 3.2 Check missingness on critical variables

Expected: no missing `tr2010_id`. Report missing `interp_rent` without imposing
an empirical threshold.

```{r validate-missingness-step2}
cat("acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated missing tr2010_id:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out$tr2010_id)), "\n")
cat("acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated missing interp_rent:", sum(is.na(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out$interp_rent)), "\n")
```

## 3.3 Check flag-variable encoding

The data-quality flags (`m_flag_*`, `zero_flag_*`, `tc_flag_*`) use numeric 0/1
values. The existing helpers store these as doubles; top-code and zero flags
retain `NA` when their source estimate is missing, while missing flags are
always observed. Geographic keys remain character and join indicators retain
their existing string/logical encodings.

```{r validate-flags-step2}
flag_cols_2024_bg_aggregated <- grep("^(m_flag_|zero_flag_|tc_flag_)", names(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out), value = TRUE)
for (f in flag_cols_2024_bg_aggregated) {
  cat("acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated", f, "-> class:", class(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out[[f]]),
      "| values:", paste(sort(unique(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out[[f]])), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

## 3.4 Summarize numeric variable distributions

Mean, min, and max for every numeric column in each output. Watch for impossible
values (negative counts, shares outside [0, 1], or rents far outside plausible
ranges).

```{r validate-numeric-step2}
print_numeric_summary(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, "acs_step2_2024_block_group_aggregated")
```

## 3.5 Check county coverage and missing/top-coded rent

The output must contain every configured county and no other destination county.
The raw diagnostic counts allocated renter-occupied units with original weights.
The saved product reports missing distribution-based `interp_rent`. Review county
differences without imposing an empirical missingness threshold. Income is retained independently of rent censoring; compare restored
income values and downstream measures using the
[income acceptance checks](notes/income_censoring.md#analyst-run-acceptance-checks).
The existing income-MOE behavior is preserved; its research ambiguity remains a
separate decision.

```{r validate-county-rent-step2}
report_tract_counties(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, target_counties, "Saved 2024 block-group-aggregated counties")
print(rent_allocation_qa_2024_bg_aggregated, n = Inf, width = Inf)
bind_rows(
  acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out |>
    transmute(county = substr(tr2010_id, 3, 5), rent_value = interp_rent,
              rent_measure = "interp_rent", product = "2024_bg_aggregated")
) |>
  group_by(product, rent_measure, county) |>
  summarise(tracts = n(), missing_rent = sum(is.na(rent_value)),
            missing_share = mean(is.na(rent_value)), .groups = "drop") |>
  print(n = Inf)
rent_share_qa_2024_bg_aggregated <- acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out |>
  select(tr2010_id, pct_miss_rent) |>
  left_join(rent_shares_2024_bg_aggregated, by = "tr2010_id")
stopifnot("Missing-rent shares must decompose into raw missing plus top-coded" = isTRUE(all.equal(
  rent_share_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$pct_miss_rent, rent_share_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$pct_m_rent + rent_share_qa_2024_bg_aggregated$pct_tc_rent,
  tolerance = 1e-10
)))
for (column in c("pct_miss_rent", "pct_m_rent", "pct_tc_rent")) {
  shares <- rent_share_qa_2024_bg_aggregated[[column]]
  stopifnot(all(is.na(shares) | (is.finite(shares) & shares >= -1e-10 & shares <= 1 + 1e-10)))
}
```

## 3.6 Check inventory completeness and reconciliation

Missing inventory must agree exactly with `inventory_incomplete` by tract key.
Every complete inventory must be finite, nonnegative, and equal to the sum of
its three separately aggregated components. Zero-contributor targets must have
zero components and inventory. These checks apply whether or not a parity
reference exists or contains inventory; no partial total is accepted.

Report affected source IDs, missing components, target IDs, and county counts
for each product. Reconcile the source-first allocated inventory against the
target-first totals over **complete targets only**, retaining the original
allocation fractions. Incomplete targets are reported separately, and the
complete-target total is not an estimate for the entire sample. The source-first
calculation adds components before weighting; the target-first calculation adds
the separately aggregated components. Original allocation pairs/weights and
occupied-renter counts must still match their earlier checks.

```{r validate-rental-inventory-step2}
assert_rental_inventory(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out, inventory_2024_bg_aggregated, "Saved 2024 block-group-aggregated inventory")
stopifnot(`Saving must preserve every 2024 block-group-aggregated value and row` = identical(acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out,
    acs_2024_bg_aggregated_interp))
print(inventory_missing_sources_2024_bg_aggregated, n = Inf, width = Inf)
print(bind_rows(`2024_bg_aggregated` = inventory_county_qa_2024_bg_aggregated, .id = "product"), n = Inf,
    width = Inf)
print(bind_rows(`2024_bg_aggregated` = reconcile_rental_inventory(acs_2024_bg_allocations, inventory_2024_bg_aggregated,
    tr2010_id, weight_col = "wt_renthu"), .id = "product"), n = Inf, width = Inf)
stopifnot("Inventory must preserve original allocation pairs and weights" = identical(
  acs_2024_bg_allocations |> select(all_of(allocation_columns)) |> arrange(bg2020_id, tr2010_id),
  xwalk_target |> select(all_of(allocation_columns)) |> arrange(bg2020_id, tr2010_id)
), "Saved occupied counts must still conserve their source contributions" = isTRUE(all.equal(
  acs_2024_bg_aggregated_out |> select(all_of(names(allocated_counts_2024_bg_aggregated))) |> arrange(tr2010_id),
  allocated_counts_2024_bg_aggregated |> arrange(tr2010_id), tolerance = 1e-10
)))
```
